AEROM_ALT_ABORT.d: Maximum allowable loss in altitude during a trick or sequence from its starting altitude.

AEROM_ANG_TC.d: This is the time over which we filter the desired roll to smooth it

AEROM_DEBUG.d: This controls the printing of extra debug information on paths

AEROM_ENTRY_RATE.n: The roll rate to use when entering a roll maneuver
AEROM_ENTRY_RATE.d: This controls how rapidly we roll into a new orientation

AEROM_ERR_COR_D.n: D gain for path error corrections
AEROM_ERR_COR_D.d: This controls how rapidly we correct back onto the desired path

AEROM_ERR_COR_P.n: P gain for path error corrections
AEROM_ERR_COR_P.d: This controls how rapidly we correct back onto the desired path

AEROM_KE_RUDD.d: Percent of rudder normally uses to sustain knife-edge at trick speed

AEROM_KE_RUDD_LK.d: Time to look ahead in the path to calculate rudder correction for bank angle

AEROM_LKAHD.d: This is how much time to look ahead in the path for calculating path rates

AEROM_MIS_ANGLE.d: When set to a non-zero value, this is the assumed direction of the mission. Otherwise the waypoint angle is used

AEROM_PATH_SCALE.d: Scale factor for Path/Box size. 0.5 would half the distances in maneuvers. Radii are unaffected.

AEROM_ROL_COR_TC.d: This is the time constant for correcting roll errors. A smaller value leads to faster roll corrections

AEROM_SPD_I.d: This controls how rapidly the throttle is raised to compensate for a speed error

AEROM_SPD_P.d: This controls how rapidly the throttle is raised to compensate for a speed error

AEROM_STALL_PIT.d: Pitch threashold for moving to final stage of stall turn

AEROM_STALL_THR.d: Amount of throttle to reduce to for a stall turn

AEROM_THR_BOOST.d: This is the extra throttle added in schedule elements marked as needing a throttle boost

AEROM_THR_LKAHD.d: This controls how far ahead we look in time along the path for the target throttle

AEROM_THR_PIT_FF.d: This controls how much extra throttle to add based on pitch ange. The value is for 90 degrees and is applied in proportion to pitch

AEROM_TIME_COR_P.n: Time constant for correction of our distance along the path
AEROM_TIME_COR_P.d: This is the time constant for correcting path position errors

AEROM_TS_I.d: This controls how rapidly two aircraft are brought back into time sync

AEROM_TS_P.d: This controls how rapidly two aircraft are brought back into time sync

AEROM_TS_RATE.n: Timesync rate of send of NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT data
AEROM_TS_RATE.d: This sets the rate we send data for time sync between aircraft

AEROM_TS_SPDMAX.d: This sets the maximum speed adjustment for time sync between aircraft

AEROM_YAW_ACCEL.d: This is maximum yaw acceleration to use

AHRS_COMP_BETA.n: AHRS Velocity Complementary Filter Beta Coefficient
AHRS_COMP_BETA.d: This controls the time constant for the cross-over frequency used to fuse AHRS (airspeed and heading) and GPS data to estimate ground velocity. Time constant is 0.1/beta. A larger time constant will use GPS data less and a small time constant will use air data less.

AHRS_CUSTOM_PIT.d: Autopilot mounting position pitch offset. Positive values = pitch up, negative values = pitch down. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.

AHRS_CUSTOM_ROLL.d: Autopilot mounting position roll offset. Positive values = roll right, negative values = roll left. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.

AHRS_CUSTOM_YAW.d: Autopilot mounting position yaw offset. Positive values = yaw right, negative values = yaw left. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.

AHRS_EKF_TYPE.n: Use NavEKF Kalman filter for attitude and position estimation
AHRS_EKF_TYPE.d: This controls which NavEKF Kalman filter version is used for attitude and position estimation

AHRS_GPS_GAIN.d: This controls how much to use the GPS to correct the attitude. This should never be set to zero for a plane as it would result in the plane losing control in turns. For a plane please use the default value of 1.0.

AHRS_GPS_MINSATS.d: Minimum number of satellites visible to use GPS for velocity based corrections attitude correction. This defaults to 6, which is about the point at which the velocity numbers from a GPS become too unreliable for accurate correction of the accelerometers.

AHRS_GPS_USE.n: AHRS use GPS for DCM navigation and position-down
AHRS_GPS_USE.d: This controls whether to use dead-reckoning or GPS based navigation. If set to 0 then the GPS won't be used for navigation, and only dead reckoning will be used. A value of zero should never be used for normal flight. Currently this affects only the DCM-based AHRS: the EKF uses GPS according to its own parameters. A value of 2 means to use GPS for height as well as position - both in DCM estimation and when determining altitude-above-home.
v: Use GPS for DCM position and height

AHRS_OPTIONS.d: This controls optional AHRS behaviour. Setting DisableDCMFallbackFW will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in fly-forward flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating. Setting DisableDCMFallbackVTOL will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in non fly-forward (VTOL) flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating. Setting DontDisableAirspeedUsingEKF disables the EKF based innovation check for airspeed consistency. Setting AutoRecordOrigin will auto-save the EKF origin to parameters when it becomes valid.

AHRS_ORIENTATION.d: Overall board orientation relative to the standard orientation for the board type. This rotates the IMU and compass readings to allow the board to be oriented in your vehicle at any 90 or 45 degree angle. The label for each option is specified in the order of rotations for that orientation. This option takes affect on next boot. After changing you will need to re-level your vehicle. Firmware versions 4.2 and prior can use a CUSTOM (100) rotation to set the AHRS_CUSTOM_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles for AHRS orientation. Later versions provide two general custom rotations which can be used, Custom 1 and Custom 2, with CUST_ROT1_ROLL/PIT/YAW or CUST_ROT2_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles.

AHRS_ORIGIN_ALT.d: AHRS last origin altitude in meters

AHRS_ORIGIN_LAT.d: AHRS last origin latitude in degrees

AHRS_ORIGIN_LON.d: AHRS last origin longitude in degrees

AHRS_ORIG_ALT.d: AHRS/EKF origin will be set to this altitude (in meters above sea level) if not already set

AHRS_ORIG_LAT.d: AHRS/EKF origin will be set to this latitude if not already set

AHRS_ORIG_LON.d: AHRS/EKF origin will be set to this longitude if not already set

AHRS_RP_P.d: This controls how fast the accelerometers correct the attitude

AHRS_TRIM_X.d: Compensates for the roll angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle roll right.

AHRS_TRIM_Y.d: Compensates for the pitch angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle pitch up/back.

AHRS_WIND_MAX.d: This sets the maximum allowable difference between ground speed and airspeed. A value of zero means to use the airspeed as is. This allows the plane to cope with a failing airspeed sensor by clipping it to groundspeed plus/minus this limit. See ARSPD_OPTIONS and ARSPD_WIND_MAX to disable airspeed sensors.

AHRS_YAW_P.d: This controls the weight the compass or GPS has on the heading. A higher value means the heading will track the yaw source (GPS or compass) more rapidly.

AIS_LIST_MAX.d: AIS list size of nearest vessels. Longer lists take longer to refresh with lower SRx_ADSB values.

AIS_TIME_OUT.d: if no updates are received in this time a vessel will be removed from the list

ALAND_WP_ALT.d: Altitude of final approach waypoint created by script

ALAND_WP_DIST.d: Distance from landing point (HOME) to final approach waypoint created by script in the opposite direction of initial takeoff

ALT_SOURCE.d: What provides altitude information for vehicle. Vehicle only assumes tracker has same altitude as vehicle's home

ARM_C_RTL_ALT_M.n: RTL_ALT_M should be a valid value
ARM_C_RTL_ALT_M.d: RTL_ALT_M should be < 120m (400ft). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_ESTOP.d: Emergency Stop disables arming. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_FENCE.d: Fences loaded but no fence enabled. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_FOLL_OFS_DEF.d: Follow offsets should not be left as default (zero) if FOLL_ENABLE = 1. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_FOLL_SYSID.d: If FOLL_ENABLE = 1, check that FOLL_SYSID has been set. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_FOLL_SYSID_X.d: If FOLL_ENABLE = 1, check that FOLL_SYSID is different to MAV_SYSID. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_MNTX_SYSID.n: Follow and Mount should follow the same vehicle
ARM_MNTX_SYSID.d: If FOLL_ENABLE = 1 and MNTx_SYSID_DEFLT is set, check that FOLL_SYSID is equal MNTx. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_P_AIRSPEED.d: Validate that AIRSPEED_STALL(if set) < MIN < CRUISE < MAX d. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_P_QRTL_ALT.n: Q_RTL_ALT should be a valid value
ARM_P_QRTL_ALT.d: Q_RTL_ALT should be < 120m (400ft). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_P_Q_FS_LAND.n: Warn if Q failsafe will land
ARM_P_Q_FS_LAND.d: Notify the user that on failsafe a QuadPlan will land. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_P_Q_FS_RTL.n: Warn if Q failsafe will QRTL
ARM_P_Q_FS_RTL.d: Notify the user that on failsafe a QuadPlan will QRTL. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_P_RTL_ALT.n: RTL_ALTITUDE should be a valid value
ARM_P_RTL_ALT.d: RTL_ALTITITUDE should be < 120m (400ft). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_P_SCALING.d: Validate that SCALING_SPEED is within 20% of AIRSPEED_CRUISE. If SCALING_SPEED changes the vehicle may need to be retuned. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_P_STALL.d: Validate that AIRSPEED_MIN is at least 25% above AIRSPEED_STALL(if set). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_RALLY.d: Rally Point more than RALLY_LIMIT_KM kilometers away. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_RTL_CLIMB.n: RTL_CLIMB_MIN should be a valid value
ARM_RTL_CLIMB.d: RTL_CLIMB_MIN should be < 120m (400ft). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_SYSID.d: Check that MAV_SYSID (or SYDID_THISMAV) has been set. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.

ARM_V_ALT_LEGAL.d: Legal max altitude for UAV/RPAS/drones in your jurisdiction

ARSPD2_AUTOCAL.d: Enables automatic adjustment of airspeed ratio during a calibration flight based on estimation of ground speed and true airspeed. New ratio saved every 2 minutes if change is > 5%. Should not be left enabled.

ARSPD2_BUS.d: Bus number of the I2C bus where the airspeed sensor is connected. May not correspond to board's I2C bus number labels. Retry another bus and reboot if airspeed sensor fails to initialize.

ARSPD2_DEVID.d: Airspeed sensor ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

ARSPD2_PIN.d: The pin number that the airspeed sensor is connected to for analog sensors. Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins".

ARSPD2_PSI_RANGE.n: The PSI range of the device
ARSPD2_PSI_RANGE.d: This parameter allows you to set the PSI (pounds per square inch) range for your sensor. You should not change this unless you examine the datasheet for your device

ARSPD2_RATIO.d: Calibrates pitot tube pressure to velocity. Increasing this value will indicate a higher airspeed at any given dynamic pressure.

ARSPD2_SKIP_CAL.n: Skip airspeed offset calibration on startup
ARSPD2_SKIP_CAL.d: This parameter allows you to skip airspeed offset calibration on startup, instead using the offset from the last calibration or requiring a manual calibration. This may be desirable if the offset variance between flights for your sensor is low and you want to avoid having to cover the pitot tube on each boot.
v: Do not require offset calibration before flight. Manual calibration should be performed during initial setup.
Do not calibrate on start up. Manual calibration must be performed once per boot.

ARSPD2_TUBE_ORDR.d: This parameter allows you to control whether the order in which the tubes are attached to your pitot tube matters. If you set this to 0 then the first (often the top) connector on the sensor needs to be the stagnation pressure (the pressure at the tip of the pitot tube). If set to 1 then the second (often the bottom) connector needs to be the stagnation pressure. If set to 2 (the default) then the airspeed driver will accept either order. The reason you may wish to specify the order is it will allow your airspeed sensor to detect if the aircraft is receiving excessive pressure on the static port compared to the stagnation port such as during a stall, which would otherwise be seen as a positive airspeed.

ARSPD2_USE.d: Enables airspeed use for automatic throttle modes and replaces control from THR_TRIM. Continues to display and log airspeed if set to 0. Uses airspeed for control if set to 1. Only uses airspeed when throttle = 0 if set to 2 (useful for gliders with airspeed sensors behind propellers).

ARSPD_WIND_GATE.d: Number of standard deviations applied to the re-enable EKF consistency check that is used when ARSPD_OPTIONS bit position 3 is set. Larger values will make the re-enabling of the airspeed sensor faster, but increase the likelihood of re-enabling a degraded sensor. The value can be tuned by using the ARSP.TR log message by setting ARSPD_WIND_GATE to a value that is higher than the value for ARSP.TR observed with a healthy airspeed sensor. Occasional transients in ARSP.TR above the value set by ARSPD_WIND_GATE can be tolerated provided they are less than 5 seconds in duration and less than 10% duty cycle.

ARSPD_WIND_MAX.n: Maximum airspeed and ground speed difference
ARSPD_WIND_MAX.d: If the difference between airspeed and ground speed is greater than this value the sensor will be marked unhealthy. Using ARSPD_OPTIONS this health value can be used to disable the sensor.

ARSPD_WIND_WARN.n: Airspeed and GPS speed difference that gives a warning
ARSPD_WIND_WARN.d: If the difference between airspeed and GPS speed is greater than this value the sensor will issue a warning. If 0 ARSPD_WIND_MAX is used.

BARO1_DEVID.d: Barometer sensor ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

BARO1_THST_SCALE.d: Thrust scaling in Pascals. This value scaled by the normalized thrust is subtracted from the barometer pressure. This is used to adjust linearly based on the thrust output for local pressure difference induced by the props.

BARO1_WCF_BCK.n: Pressure error coefficient in negative X direction (backwards)
BARO1_WCF_BCK.d: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a negative wind relative velocity along the X body axis. If the baro height estimate rises during backwards flight, then this will be a negative number. Multirotors can use this feature only if using EKF3 and if the EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X and EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y parameters have been tuned.

BARO1_WCF_DN.n: Pressure error coefficient in negative Z direction (down)
BARO1_WCF_DN.d: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a negative wind relative velocity along the Z body axis. If the baro height estimate rises above truth height during descending flight (or forward flight with a high backwards lean angle, eg braking manoeuvre), then this should be a negative number. Multirotors can use this feature only if using EKF3 and if the EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X and EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y parameters have been tuned.

BARO_ALTERR_MAX.d: This is the maximum acceptable altitude discrepancy between GPS altitude and barometric presssure altitude calculated against a standard atmosphere for arming checks to pass. If you are getting an arming error due to this parameter then you may have a faulty or substituted barometer. A common issue is vendors replacing a MS5611 in a "Pixhawk" with a MS5607. If you have that issue then please see BARO_OPTIONS parameter to force the MS5611 to be treated as a MS5607. This check is disabled if the value is zero.

BARO_ALT_OFFSET.d: altitude offset in meters added to barometric altitude. This is used to allow for automatic adjustment of the base barometric altitude by a ground station equipped with a barometer. The value is added to the barometric altitude read by the aircraft. It is automatically reset to 0 when the barometer is calibrated on each reboot or when a preflight calibration is performed.

BARO_EXT_BUS.d: This selects the bus number for looking for an I2C barometer. When set to -1 it will probe all external i2c buses based on the BARO_PROBE_EXT parameter.

BARO_FIELD_ELV.d: User provided field elevation in meters. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. Changes to this parameter will only be used when disarmed. A value of 0 means the EKF origin height is used for takeoff height above sea level.

BARO_FLTR_RNG.n: Range in which sample is accepted
BARO_FLTR_RNG.d: This sets the range around the average value that new samples must be within to be accepted. This can help reduce the impact of noise on sensors that are on long I2C cables. The value is a percentage from the average value. A value of zero disables this filter.

BARO_GND_TEMP.d: User provided ambient ground temperature in degrees Celsius. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. A value of 0 means use the internal measurement ambient temperature.

BARO_PRIMARY.d: This selects which barometer will be the primary if multiple barometers are found

BARO_PROBE_EXT.d: This sets which types of external i2c barometer to look for. It is a bitmask of barometer types. The I2C buses to probe is based on BARO_EXT_BUS. If BARO_EXT_BUS is -1 then it will probe all external buses, otherwise it will probe just the bus number given in BARO_EXT_BUS.

BARO_SPEC_GRAV.d: This sets the specific gravity of the fluid when flying an underwater ROV.

BATT2_AMP_OFFSET.d: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor

BATT2_AMP_PERVLT.d: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to.

BATT2_ARM_MAH.d: Battery capacity remaining which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any capacity. Note that execept for smart batteries rebooting the vehicle will always reset the remaining capacity estimate, which can lead to this check not providing sufficent protection, it is recommended to always use this in conjunction with the BATT2_ARM_VOLT parameter.

BATT2_ARM_VOLT.d: Battery voltage level which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any voltage.

BATT2_CAPACITY.d: Capacity of the battery in mAh when full

BATT2_CHANNEL.d: INA3221 channel to return data for

BATT2_CRT_MAH.d: Battery capacity at which the critical battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

BATT2_CRT_VOLT.d: Battery voltage that triggers a critical battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATT2_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

BATT2_CURR_MULT.d: Multiplier applied to all current related reports to allow for adjustment if no UAVCAN param access or current splitting applications

BATT2_CURR_PIN.d: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for Current monitoring on AD7091R5.

BATT2_ESC_INDEX.n: ESC Telemetry Index to write to
BATT2_ESC_INDEX.d: ESC Telemetry Index to write voltage, current, consumption and temperature data to. Use 0 to disable.

BATT2_ESC_MASK.d: If 0 all connected ESCs will be used. If non-zero, only those selected in will be used.

BATT2_FL_FLTR.d: Filter frequency in Hertz where a low pass filter is used. This is used to filter out tank slosh from the fuel level reading. A value of -1 disables the filter and unfiltered voltage is used to determine the fuel level. The suggested values at in the range of 0.2 Hz to 0.5 Hz.

BATT2_FL_PIN.d: Analog input pin that fuel level sensor is connected to.Analog Airspeed or RSSI ports can be used for Analog input( some autopilots provide others also). Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins".

BATT2_FL_VLT_MIN.d: The voltage seen on the analog pin when the fuel tank is empty. Note: For this type of battery monitor, the voltage seen by the analog pin is displayed as battery voltage on a GCS.

BATT2_FL_V_MULT.d: Voltage multiplier to determine what the full tank voltage reading is. This is calculated as 1 / (Voltage_Full - Voltage_Empty) Note: For this type of battery monitor, the voltage seen by the analog pin is displayed as battery voltage on a GCS.

BATT2_FS_CRT_ACT.d: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a critical battery failsafe

BATT2_FS_LOW_ACT.d: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a low battery failsafe

BATT2_FS_VOLTSRC.d: Voltage type used for detection of low voltage event

BATT2_I2C_ADDR.d: Battery monitor I2C address. If this is zero then probe list of supported addresses

BATT2_LOW_MAH.d: Battery capacity at which the low battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

BATT2_LOW_TIMER.d: This is the timeout in seconds before a low voltage event will be triggered. For aircraft with low C batteries it may be necessary to raise this in order to cope with low voltage on long takeoffs. A value of zero disables low voltage errors.

BATT2_LOW_VOLT.d: Battery voltage that triggers a low battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATT2_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

BATT2_MAX_AMPS.d: This controls the maximum current the INA239 sensor will work with.

BATT2_MAX_VOLT.d: Maximum voltage of battery. Provides scaling of current versus voltage

BATT2_MONITOR.d: Controls enabling monitoring of the battery's voltage and current

BATT2_OPTIONS.d: This sets options to change the behaviour of the battery monitor
b: MPPT reports input voltage and current
Send resistance compensated voltage to GCS
Allow DroneCAN InfoAux to be from a different CAN node
Battery is for internal autopilot use only
Sum monitor measures minimum voltage instead of average
Allow DroneCAN dynamic node update on hot-swap

BATT2_SERIAL_NUM.d: Battery serial number, automatically filled in for SMBus batteries, otherwise will be -1. With DroneCan it is the battery_id.

BATT2_SHUNT.d: This sets the shunt resistor used in the device

BATT2_SUM_MASK.d: 0: sum of remaining battery monitors, If none 0 sum of specified monitors. Current will be summed and voltages averaged.

BATT2_VLT_OFFSET.d: Voltage offset on voltage pin. This allows for an offset due to a diode. This voltage is subtracted before the scaling is applied

BATT2_VOLT_MULT.d: Used to convert the voltage of the voltage sensing pin (BATT2_VOLT_PIN) to the actual battery's voltage (pin_voltage * VOLT_MULT).

BATT2_VOLT_PIN.n: Battery Voltage sensing pin on the AD7091R5 Ic
BATT2_VOLT_PIN.d: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for voltage monitoring on AD7091R5.

BATT2_WATT_MAX.d: If battery wattage (voltage * current) exceeds this value then the system will reduce max throttle (THR_MAX, TKOFF_THR_MAX and THR_MIN for reverse thrust) to satisfy this limit. This helps limit high current to low C rated batteries regardless of battery voltage. The max throttle will slowly grow back to THR_MAX (or TKOFF_THR_MAX ) and THR_MIN if demanding the current max and under the watt max. Use 0 to disable.

This helps limit high current to low C rated batteries regardless of battery voltage. The max throttle will slowly grow back to THR_MAX (or TKOFF_THR_MAX ) and THR_MIN if demanding the current max and under the watt max. Use 0 to disable.

BATTA_AMP_OFFSET.d: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor

BATTA_AMP_PERVLT.d: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to.

BATTA_ARM_MAH.d: Battery capacity remaining which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any capacity. Note that execept for smart batteries rebooting the vehicle will always reset the remaining capacity estimate, which can lead to this check not providing sufficent protection, it is recommended to always use this in conjunction with the BATTA_ARM_VOLT parameter.

BRD_ALT_CONFIG.d: Select an alternative hardware configuration. A value of zero selects the default configuration for this board. Other values are board specific. Please see the documentation for your board for details on any alternative configuration values that may be available.

BRD_BOOT_DELAY.d: This adds a delay in milliseconds to boot to ensure peripherals initialise fully

BRD_HEAT_LOWMGN.d: Arming check will fail if temp is lower than this margin below BRD_HEAT_TARG. 0 disables the low temperature check

BRD_HEAT_TARG.d: Board heater target temperature for boards with controllable heating units. Set to -1 to disable the heater, please reboot after setting to -1.

BRD_IDLE_STATS.n: Capture and calculate true CPU load using idle threads
BRD_IDLE_STATS.d: Capture and calculate true CPU load using idle threads

BRD_IO_DSHOT.d: This loads the DShot firmware on the IO co-processor

BRD_IO_ENABLE.d: This allows for the IO co-processor on boards with an IOMCU to be disabled. Setting to 2 will enable the IOMCU but not attempt to update firmware on startup

b: Write protect firmware flash on reboot
Write protect bootloader flash on reboot
Disable board arming gpio output change on arm/disarm

BRD_PWM_VOLT_SEL.d: This sets the voltage max for PWM output pulses. 0 for 3.3V and 1 for 5V output. On boards with an IOMCU that support this parameter this option only affects the 8 main outputs, not the 6 auxiliary outputs. Using 5V output can help to reduce the impact of ESC noise interference corrupting signals to the ESCs.

BRD_RADIO_ABLVL.d: This sets the minimum RSSI of an auto-bind packet for it to be accepted. This should be set so that auto-bind will only happen at short range to minimise the change of an auto-bind happening accidentially

BRD_RADIO_ABTIME.d: When non-zero this sets the time with no transmitter packets before we start looking for auto-bind packets.

BRD_RADIO_BZOFS.d: Set transmitter buzzer note adjustment (adjust frequency up)

BRD_RADIO_FCCTST.n: Put radio into FCC test mode
BRD_RADIO_FCCTST.d: If this is enabled then the radio will continuously transmit as required for FCC testing. The transmit channel is set by the value of the parameter. The radio will not work for RC input while this is enabled

BRD_RADIO_PPSCH.d: Channel to show received packet-per-second rate, or zero for disabled

BRD_RADIO_SIGCH.d: Channel to show receive RSSI signal strength, or zero for disabled

BRD_RADIO_STKMD.d: This selects between different stick input modes. The default is mode2, which has throttle on the left stick and pitch on the right stick. You can instead set mode1, which has throttle on the right stick and pitch on the left stick.

BRD_RADIO_TELEM.d: If this is non-zero then telemetry packets will be sent over DSM

BRD_RADIO_TESTCH.n: Set radio to factory test channel
BRD_RADIO_TESTCH.d: This sets the radio to a fixed test channel for factory testing. Using a fixed channel avoids the need for binding in factory testing.

BRD_RADIO_TPPSCH.d: Channel to show telemetry packets-per-second value, as received at TX

BRD_RADIO_TSIGCH.n: RSSI value channel for telemetry data on transmitter
BRD_RADIO_TSIGCH.d: Channel to show telemetry RSSI value as received by TX

BRD_RADIO_TXMAX.d: Set transmitter maximum transmit power (from 1 to 8)

BRD_RADIO_TXPOW.d: Set telemetry transmit power. This is the power level (from 1 to 8) for telemetry packets sent from the RX to the TX

BRD_RADIO_TYPE.n: Set type of direct attached radio
BRD_RADIO_TYPE.d: This enables support for direct attached radio receivers

BRD_RTC_TYPES.d: Specifies which sources of UTC time will be accepted

BRD_RTC_TZ_MIN.d: Adds offset in +- minutes from UTC to calculate local time

BRD_SAFETYENABLE.d: This controls the default state of the safety switch at startup. When set to 1 the safety switch will start in the safe state (flashing) at boot. When set to zero the safety switch will start in the unsafe state (solid) at startup. Note that if a safety switch is fitted the user can still control the safety state after startup using the switch. The safety state can also be controlled in software using a MAVLink message.
BRD_SAFETYENABLE.n: Enable use of safety arming switch

BRD_SAFETYOPTION.d: This controls the activation of the safety button. It allows you to control if the safety button can be used for safety enable and/or disable, and whether the button is only active when disarmed
b: Force safety on when the aircraft disarms

BRD_SAFETY_DEFLT.d: This controls the default state of the safety switch at startup. When set to 1 the safety switch will start in the safe state (flashing) at boot. When set to zero the safety switch will start in the unsafe state (solid) at startup. Note that if a safety switch is fitted the user can still control the safety state after startup using the switch. The safety state can also be controlled in software using a MAVLink message.

BRD_SAFETY_MASK.n: Outputs which ignore the safety switch state
BRD_SAFETY_MASK.d: A bitmask which controls what outputs can move while the safety switch has not been pressed

BRD_SBUS_OUT.d: This sets the SBUS output frame rate in Hz

BRD_SD_FENCE.d: This sets the amount of storage in kilobytes reserved on the microsd card in fence.stg for fence storage.

BRD_SD_MISSION.d: This sets the amount of storage in kilobytes reserved on the microsd card in mission.stg for waypoint storage. Each waypoint uses 15 bytes.

BRD_SD_SLOWDOWN.d: This is a scaling factor to slow down microSD operation. It can be used on flight board and microSD card combinations where full speed is not reliable. For normal full speed operation a value of 0 should be used.

Note that the PX4v1 does not have hardware flow control pins on this port, so you should leave this disabled.

CAN_D1_PROTOCOL2.d: Secondary protocol with 11 bit CAN addressing

COMPASS_EXTERNAL.n: Compass is attached via an external cable
COMPASS_EXTERNAL.d: Configure compass so it is attached externally. This is auto-detected on most boards. Set to 1 if the compass is externally connected. When externally connected the COMPASS_ORIENT option operates independently of the AHRS_ORIENTATION board orientation option. If set to 0 or 1 then auto-detection by bus connection can override the value. If set to 2 then auto-detection will be disabled.

COMPASS_FLTR_RNG.n: Range in which sample is accepted
COMPASS_FLTR_RNG.d: This sets the range around the average value that new samples must be within to be accepted. This can help reduce the impact of noise on sensors that are on long I2C cables. The value is a percentage from the average value. A value of zero disables this filter.

COMPASS_LEARN.d: Enable or disable the automatic learning of compass offsets. You can enable learning either using a compass-only method that is suitable only for fixed wing aircraft or using the offsets learnt by the active EKF state estimator. If this option is enabled then the learnt offsets are saved when you disarm the vehicle. If InFlight learning is enabled then the compass with automatically start learning once a flight starts (must be armed). While InFlight learning is running you cannot use position control modes.

b: Allow missing DroneCAN compasses to be automaticaly replaced (calibration still required)

COMPASS_ORIENT.d: The orientation of the first external compass relative to the vehicle frame. This value will be ignored unless this compass is set as an external compass. When set correctly in the northern hemisphere, pointing the nose and right side down should increase the MagX and MagY values respectively. Rolling the vehicle upside down should decrease the MagZ value. For southern hemisphere, switch increase and decrease. NOTE: For internal compasses, AHRS_ORIENT is used. The label for each option is specified in the order of rotations for that orientation. Firmware versions 4.2 and prior can use a CUSTOM (100) rotation to set the COMPASS_CUS_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles for Compass orientation. Later versions provide two general custom rotations which can be used, Custom 1 and Custom 2, with CUST_1_ROLL/PIT/YAW or CUST_2_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles.

COMPASS_ORIENT2.d: The orientation of a second external compass relative to the vehicle frame. This value will be ignored unless this compass is set as an external compass. When set correctly in the northern hemisphere, pointing the nose and right side down should increase the MagX and MagY values respectively. Rolling the vehicle upside down should decrease the MagZ value. For southern hemisphere, switch increase and decrease. NOTE: For internal compasses, AHRS_ORIENT is used. The label for each option is specified in the order of rotations for that orientation. Firmware versions 4.2 and prior can use a CUSTOM (100) rotation to set the COMPASS_CUS_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles for Compass orientation. Later versions provide two general custom rotations which can be used, Custom 1 and Custom 2, with CUST_1_ROLL/PIT/YAW or CUST_2_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles.

COMPASS_ORIENT3.d: The orientation of a third external compass relative to the vehicle frame. This value will be ignored unless this compass is set as an external compass. When set correctly in the northern hemisphere, pointing the nose and right side down should increase the MagX and MagY values respectively. Rolling the vehicle upside down should decrease the MagZ value. For southern hemisphere, switch increase and decrease. NOTE: For internal compasses, AHRS_ORIENT is used. The label for each option is specified in the order of rotations for that orientation. Firmware versions 4.2 and prior can use a CUSTOM (100) rotation to set the COMPASS_CUS_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles for Compass orientation. Later versions provide two general custom rotations which can be used, Custom 1 and Custom 2, with CUST_1_ROLL/PIT/YAW or CUST_2_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles.
