MAV_GCS_SYSID.d: This sets what MAVLink source system IDs are accepted for GCS failsafe handling, RC overrides and manual control. When MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI is less than MAV_GCS_SYSID then only this value is considered to be a GCS. When MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI is greater than or equal to MAV_GCS_SYSID then the range of values between MAV_GCS_SYSID and MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI (inclusive) are all treated as valid GCS MAVLink system IDs

MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI.d: Upper limit of MAVLink source system IDs considered to be from the GCS. When this is less than MAV_GCS_SYSID then only MAV_GCS_SYSID is used as GCS ID. When this is greater than or equal to MAV_GCS_SYSID then the range of values from MAV_GCS_SYSID to MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI (inclusive) is treated as a GCS ID.

MAV_OPTIONS.d: Alters various behaviour of the MAVLink interface
b: Accept MAVLink only from system IDs given by MAV_SYSID_GCS and MAV_SYSID_GCS_HI

MAV_SYSID.n: MAVLink system ID of this vehicle
MAV_SYSID.d: Allows setting an individual MAVLink system id for this vehicle to distinguish it from others on the same network.

MAV_TELEM_DELAY.d: The amount of time (in seconds) to delay radio telemetry to prevent an Xbee bricking on power up

MAV_UPDATE_RATE.d: The rate at which Mavlink updates position and baro data

MIN_REVERSE_TIME.n: Minimum time to apply a yaw reversal
MIN_REVERSE_TIME.d: When the tracker detects it has reached the limit of servo movement in yaw it will reverse and try moving to the other extreme of yaw. This parameter controls the minimum time it should reverse for. It is used to cope with trackers that have a significant lag in movement to ensure they do move all the way around.

MODE.d: 0: The sensor will save the fuel consumption across power resets. 1: The sensor will reset the power consumption.

MSP_OPTIONS.d: A bitmask to set some MSP specific options: EnableTelemetryMode-allows "push" mode telemetry when only rx line of OSD ic connected to autopilot, EnableBTFLFonts-uses indexes corresponding to Betaflight fonts if OSD uses those instead of ArduPilot fonts. EnableINAVFonts uses INAV fonts and overrides EnableBTFLFonts if that option is enabled.

MSP_OSD_NCELLS.d: Used for average cell voltage calculation

NET_NETMASK.d: Allows setting static subnet mask. The value is a count of consecutive bits. Examples: 24 = 255.255.255.0, 16 = 255.255.0.0

NET_P1_TYPE.d: Port type for network serial port. For the two client types a valid destination IP address must be set. For the two server types either 0.0.0.0 or a local address can be used. The UDP client type will use broadcast if the IP is set to 255.255.255.255 and will use UDP multicast if the IP is in the multicast address range.

NET_P2_TYPE.d: Port type for network serial port. For the two client types a valid destination IP address must be set. For the two server types either 0.0.0.0 or a local address can be used. The UDP client type will use broadcast if the IP is set to 255.255.255.255 and will use UDP multicast if the IP is in the multicast address range.

NET_P3_TYPE.d: Port type for network serial port. For the two client types a valid destination IP address must be set. For the two server types either 0.0.0.0 or a local address can be used. The UDP client type will use broadcast if the IP is set to 255.255.255.255 and will use UDP multicast if the IP is in the multicast address range.

NET_P4_TYPE.d: Port type for network serial port. For the two client types a valid destination IP address must be set. For the two server types either 0.0.0.0 or a local address can be used. The UDP client type will use broadcast if the IP is set to 255.255.255.255 and will use UDP multicast if the IP is in the multicast address range.

NMEA_MSG_EN.d: This is a bitmask of enabled NMEA messages. All messages will be sent consecutively at the same rate interval

NMEA_RATE_MS.d: NMEA Output rate. This controls the interval at which all the enabled NMEA messages are sent. Most NMEA systems expect 100ms (10Hz) or slower.

NTF_BUZZ_ON_LVL.d: Specifies pin level that indicates buzzer should play

NTF_BUZZ_PIN.d: Enables to connect active buzzer to arbitrary pin. Requires 3-pin buzzer or additional MOSFET! Some the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

NTF_BUZZ_TYPES.d: Controls what types of Buzzer will be enabled

NTF_BUZZ_VOLUME.d: Control the volume of the buzzer

NTF_DISPLAY_TYPE.d: This sets up the type of on-board I2C display. Disabled by default.

NTF_LED_BRIGHT.d: Select the RGB LED brightness level. When USB is connected brightness will never be higher than low regardless of the setting.

NTF_LED_LEN.d: The number of Serial LED's to use for notifications (NeoPixel's and ProfiLED)

NTF_LED_OVERRIDE.n: Specifies colour source for the RGBLed
NTF_LED_OVERRIDE.d: Specifies the source for the colours and brightness for the LED. OutbackChallenge conforms to the MedicalExpress (https://uavchallenge.org/medical-express/) rules, essentially "Green" is disarmed (safe-to-approach), "Red" is armed (not safe-to-approach). Traffic light is a simplified color set, red when armed, yellow when the safety switch is not surpressing outputs (but disarmed), and green when outputs are surpressed and disarmed, the LED will blink faster if disarmed and failing arming checks.

NTF_LED_TYPES.d: Controls what types of LEDs will be enabled

NTF_OREO_THEME.d: Enable/Disable Solo Oreo LED driver, 0 to disable, 1 for Aircraft theme, 2 for Rover theme

ONOFF_PITCH_MINT.d: Minimum amount of time in seconds to move in pitch

ONOFF_PITCH_RATE.d: Rate of change of pitch in degrees/second for on/off servos

ONOFF_YAW_MINT.d: Minimum amount of time in seconds to move in yaw

ONOFF_YAW_RATE.d: Rate of change of yaw in degrees/second for on/off servos

PITCH2SRV_D.d: Pitch axis controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired pitch angle vs actual pitch angle

PITCH2SRV_D_FF.d: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target

PITCH2SRV_FLTD.n: Pitch axis controller derivative frequency in Hz
PITCH2SRV_FLTD.d: Pitch axis controller derivative frequency in Hz

PITCH2SRV_FLTE.n: Pitch axis controller error frequency in Hz
PITCH2SRV_FLTE.d: Pitch axis controller error frequency in Hz

PITCH2SRV_FLTT.n: Pitch axis controller target frequency in Hz
PITCH2SRV_FLTT.d: Pitch axis controller target frequency in Hz

PITCH2SRV_I.d: Pitch axis controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired pitch angle vs actual pitch angle

PITCH2SRV_IMAX.n: Pitch axis controller I gain maximum
PITCH2SRV_IMAX.d: Pitch axis controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum pwm change that the I gain will output

PITCH2SRV_P.d: Pitch axis controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired pitch angle and actual pitch angle into a pitch servo pwm change

PITCH2SRV_PDMX.n: Pitch axis controller PD sum maximum
PITCH2SRV_PDMX.d: Pitch axis controller PD sum maximum. The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output

PITCH2SRV_SMAX.d: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

PITCH_MAX.d: The highest angle the pitch can reach

PITCH_MIN.d: The lowest angle the pitch can reach

PITCH_SLEW_TIME.n: Time for pitch to slew through its full range
PITCH_SLEW_TIME.d: This controls how rapidly the tracker will change the servo output for pitch. It is set as the number of seconds to do a full range of pitch movement. You can use this parameter to slow the trackers movements, which may help with some types of trackers. A value of zero will allow for unlimited servo movement per update.

PITCH_TRIM.d: Amount of extra pitch to add when tracking. This allows for small adjustments for a badly calibrated barometer.

PLND_ALT_CUTOFF.d: The altitude (rangefinder distance) below which we stop using the precision landing sensor and continue landing

POI_DIST_MAX.d: POI's max distance (in meters) from the vehicle

PORT.d: Which Scripting serial port the sensor is connected at.

PREV_RC_FUNC.d: RCn_OPTION number to used to trigger parameter reversion

QUIK_ANGLE_MAX.n: maximum angle error for tune abort
QUIK_ANGLE_MAX.d: If while tuning the angle error goes over this limit then the tune will aborts to prevent a bad oscillation in the case of the tuning algorithm failing. If you get an error "Tuning: attitude error ABORTING" and you think it is a false positive then you can either raise this parameter or you can try increasing the QUIK_DOUBLE_TIME to do the tune more slowly. A value of zero disables this check.

QUIK_AUTO_FILTER.d: When enabled the PID filter settings are automatically set based on INS_GYRO_FILTER

QUIK_AUTO_SAVE.d: Number of seconds after completion of tune to auto-save. This is useful when using a 2 position switch for quicktune

QUIK_DOUBLE_TIME.d: Time to double a tuning parameter. Raise this for a slower tune.

QUIK_GAIN_MARGIN.d: Reduction in gain after oscillation detected. Raise this number to get a more conservative tune

QUIK_MAX_REDUCE.d: This controls how much quicktune is allowed to lower gains from the original gains. If the vehicle already has a reasonable tune and is not oscillating then you can set this to zero to prevent gain reductions. The default of 20% is reasonable for most vehicles. Using a maximum gain reduction lowers the chance of an angle P oscillation happening if quicktune gets a false positive oscillation at a low gain, which can result in very low rate gains and a dangerous angle P oscillation.

QUIK_OPTIONS.d: Additional options. When the Two Position Switch option is enabled then a high switch position will start the tune, low will disable the tune. you should also set a QUIK_AUTO_SAVE time so that you will be able to save the tune.

QUIK_OSC_SMAX.d: Threshold for oscillation detection. A lower value will lead to a more conservative tune.

QUIK_RC_FUNC.d: RCn_OPTION number to use to control tuning stop/start/save

QUIK_RP_PI_RATIO.d: Ratio between P and I gains for roll and pitch. Raise this to get a lower I gain

QUIK_YAW_D_MAX.d: Maximum value for yaw D gain

QUIK_YAW_P_MAX.d: Maximum value for yaw P gain

QUIK_Y_PI_RATIO.d: Ratio between P and I gains for yaw. Raise this to get a lower I gain

RCK_DEBUG.d: Sends Rockblock debug text to GCS via statustexts

RCK_ENABLE.d: Enables the Rockblock sending and recieving

RCK_FORCEHL.d: Automatically enables High Latency mode if not already enabled

RCK_PERIOD.d: When in High Latency mode, send Rockblock updates every N seconds

RCK_TIMEOUT.n: GCS timeout to start sendin Rockblock messages
RCK_TIMEOUT.d: If RCK_FORCEHL=2, this is the number of seconds of GCS timeout until High Latency mode is auto-enabled

RC_FS_TIMEOUT.d: RC failsafe will trigger this many seconds after loss of RC

b: Ignore Receiver Failsafe bit but allow other RC failsafes if setup
Skip the arming check for neutral Roll/Pitch/Yaw sticks
Suppress CRSF mode/rate message for ELRS systems
Use Link Quality for RSSI with CRSF
Annotate CRSF flight mode with * on disarm

RC_OVERRIDE_TIME.d: Timeout after which RC overrides will no longer be used, and RC input will resume, 0 will disable RC overrides, -1 will never timeout, and continue using overrides until they are disabled

RC_PROTOCOLS.d: Bitmask of enabled RC protocols. Allows narrowing the protocol detection to only specific types of RC receivers which can avoid issues with incorrect detection. Set to 1 to enable all protocols.

SCR_THD_PRIORITY.d: This sets the priority of the scripting thread. This is normally set to a low priority to prevent scripts from interfering with other parts of the system. Advanced users can change this priority if scripting needs to be prioritised for realtime applications. WARNING: changing this parameter can impact the stability of your flight controller. The scipting thread priority in this parameter is chosen based on a set of system level priorities for other subsystems. It is strongly recommended that you use the lowest priority that is sufficient for your application. Note that all scripts run at the same priority, so if you raise this priority you must carefully audit all lua scripts for behaviour that does not interfere with the operation of the system.

SERIAL_PASS1.d: This sets one side of pass-through between two serial ports. Once both sides are set then all data received on either port will be passed to the other port

SERIAL_PASS2.d: This sets one side of pass-through between two serial ports. Once both sides are set then all data received on either port will be passed to the other port. This parameter is normally reset to -1 on reboot, disabling passthrough. If SERIAL_PASSTIMO is set to -1 then it is not reset on reboot.

SERIAL_PASSTIMO.d: This sets a timeout for serial pass-through in seconds. When the pass-through is enabled by setting the SERIAL_PASS1 and SERIAL_PASS2 parameters then it remains in effect until no data comes from the first port for SERIAL_PASSTIMO seconds. This allows the port to revent to its normal usage (such as MAVLink connection to a GCS) when it is no longer needed. A value of 0 means no timeout. A value of -1 means no timeout and the SERIAL_PASS2 parameter is not reset on reboot.

SERVO_32_ENABLE.d: This allows for up to 32 outputs, enabling parameters for outputs above 16

SERVO_AUTO_TRIM.d: This enables automatic servo trim in flight. Servos will be trimed in stabilized flight modes when the aircraft is close to level. Changes to servo trim will be saved every 10 seconds and will persist between flights. The automatic trim won't go more than 20% away from a centered trim.

SERVO_BLH_3DMASK.d: Mask of channels which are dynamically reversible. This is used to configure ESCs in '3D' mode, allowing for the motor to spin in either direction. Note that setting an ESC as reversible with this option on AM32 will result in the forward direction of the ESC changing. You can combine with parameter with the SERVO_BLH_RVMASK parameter to maintain the same direction when the ESC is in 3D mode as it has in unidirectional (non-3D) mode.

SERVO_BLH_AUTO.n: BLHeli pass-thru auto-enable for multicopter motors
SERVO_BLH_AUTO.d: If set to 1 this auto-enables BLHeli pass-thru support for all multicopter motors

SERVO_BLH_BDMASK.n: BLHeli bitmask of bi-directional dshot channels
SERVO_BLH_BDMASK.d: Mask of channels which support bi-directional dshot telemetry. This is used for ESCs which have firmware that supports bi-directional dshot allowing fast rpm telemetry values to be returned for the harmonic notch.

SERVO_BLH_DEBUG.d: When set to 1 this enabled verbose debugging output over MAVLink when the blheli protocol is active. This can be used to diagnose failures.

SERVO_BLH_MASK.d: Enable of BLHeli pass-thru servo protocol support to specific channels. This mask is in addition to motors enabled using SERVO_BLH_AUTO (if any)

SERVO_BLH_OTYPE.d: When set to a non-zero value this overrides the output type for the output channels given by SERVO_BLH_MASK. This can be used to enable DShot on outputs that are not part of the multicopter motors group.

SERVO_BLH_POLES.d: This allows calculation of true RPM from ESC's eRPM. The default is 14.

SERVO_BLH_PORT.d: This sets the mavlink channel to use for blheli pass-thru. The channel number is determined by the number of serial ports configured to use mavlink. So 0 is always the console, 1 is the next serial port using mavlink, 2 the next after that and so on.

SERVO_BLH_RVMASK.d: Mask of channels which are reversed. This is used to configure ESCs to reverse motor direction. Note that when combined with SERVO_BLH_3DMASK this will change what direction is considered to be forward.

SERVO_BLH_TEST.d: Setting SERVO_BLH_TEST to a motor number enables an internal test of the BLHeli ESC protocol to the corresponding ESC. The debug output is displayed on the USB console.

SERVO_BLH_TMOUT.d: This sets the inactivity timeout for the BLHeli protocol in seconds. If no packets are received in this time normal MAVLink operations are resumed. A value of 0 means no timeout

SERVO_BLH_TRATE.d: This sets the rate in Hz for requesting telemetry from ESCs. It is the rate per ESC. Setting to zero disables telemetry requests

SERVO_DSHOT_ESC.d: DShot ESC type for all outputs. The ESC type affects the range of DShot commands available and the bit widths used. None means that no dshot commands will be executed. Some ESC types support Extended DShot Telemetry (EDT) which allows telemetry other than RPM data to be returned when using bi-directional dshot. If you enable EDT you must install EDT capable firmware for correct operation.

SERVO_DSHOT_RATE.d: DShot output rate for all outputs as a multiple of the loop rate. 0 sets the output rate to be fixed at 1Khz for low loop rates. This value should never be set below 500Hz.

SERVO_FTW_MASK.d: Servo channel mask specifying FETtec ESC output.

SERVO_FTW_RVMASK.d: Servo channel mask to reverse rotation of FETtec ESC outputs.

SERVO_GPIO_MASK.d: Bitmask of outputs which will be available as GPIOs. Any output with either the function set to -1 or with the corresponding bit set in this mask will be available for use as a GPIO pin

SERVO_PITCH_TYPE.n: Type of servo system being used for pitch
SERVO_PITCH_TYPE.d: This allows selection of position servos or on/off servos for pitch

SERVO_RATE.d: Default output rate in Hz for all PWM outputs.

SERVO_RC_FS_MSK.d: Bitmask of scaled passthru output channels which will be set to their trim value during rc failsafe instead of holding their last position before failsafe.

SERVO_ROB_POSMAX.d: Position maximum at servo max value. This should be within the position control range of the servos, normally 0 to 4095

SERVO_ROB_POSMIN.d: Position minimum at servo min value. This should be within the position control range of the servos, normally 0 to 4095

SERVO_SBUS_RATE.d: This sets the SBUS output frame rate in Hz.

SERVO_VOLZ_MASK.d: Enable of volz servo protocol to specific channels

SERVO_VOLZ_RANGE.d: Range to map between 1000 and 2000 PWM. Default value of 200 gives full +-100 deg range of extended position command. This results in 0.2 deg movement per US change in PWM. If the full range is not needed it can be reduced to increase resolution. 40 deg range gives 0.04 deg movement per US change in PWM, this is higher resolution than possible with the VOLZ protocol so further reduction in range will not improve resolution. Reduced range does allow PWMs outside the 1000 to 2000 range, with 40 deg range 750 PWM results in a angle of -30 deg, 2250 would be +30 deg. This is still limited by the 200 deg maximum range of the actuator.

SERVO_YAW_TYPE.n: Type of servo system being used for yaw
SERVO_YAW_TYPE.d: This allows selection of position servos or on/off servos for yaw

SHIP_AUTO_OFS.d: Settings this parameter to one triggers an automatic follow offset calculation based on current position of the vehicle and the landing target. NOTE: This parameter will auto-reset to zero once the offset has been calculated.

SHIP_LAND_ANGLE.d: Angle from the stern of the ship for landing approach. Use this to ensure that on a go-around that ship superstructure and cables are avoided. A value of zero means to approach from the rear of the ship. A value of 90 means the landing will approach from the port (left) side of the ship. A value of -90 will mean approaching from the starboard (right) side of the ship. A value of 180 will approach from the bow of the ship. This parameter is combined with the sign of the RTL_RADIUS parameter to determine the holdoff pattern. If RTL_RADIUS is positive then a clockwise loiter is performed, if RTL_RADIUS is negative then a counter-clockwise loiter is used.

SIM_MAG_ALY_HGT.d: Height above ground where anomally strength has decayed to 1/8 of the ground level value

SIM_MAG_ALY_X.n: NED anomaly vector at ground level
SIM_MAG_ALY_X.d: Simulates localized magnetic field distortions at ground level that decays with altitude. (X-axis)

SIM_MAG_ALY_Y.n: NED anomaly vector at ground level
SIM_MAG_ALY_Y.d: Simulates localized magnetic field distortions at ground level that decays with altitude. (Y-axis)

SIM_MAG_ALY_Z.n: NED anomaly vector at ground level
SIM_MAG_ALY_Z.d: Simulates localized magnetic field distortions at ground level that decays with altitude. (Z-axis)

SIM_MAG_MOT_X.d: Simulates distortion of magnetometer readings caused by motor current (X-axis)

SIM_MAG_MOT_Y.d: Simulates distortion of magnetometer readings caused by motor current (Y-axis)

SIM_MAG_MOT_Z.d: Simulates distortion of magnetometer readings caused by motor current (Z-axis)

SIM_MAG_RND.d: Scaling factor for simulated vibration from motors

SIM_MAG_SAVE_IDS.d: This forces saving of compass devids on startup so that simulated compasses start as calibrated

SIM_OH_MASK.d: channels which are passed through to actual hardware when running sim on actual hardware

SIM_OH_RELAY_MSK.d: Allow relay output operation when running SIM-on-hardware

SIM_OSD_COLUMNS.n: Simulated OSD number of text columns

SIM_OSD_ROWS.n: Simulated OSD number of text rows

SIM_PARA_ENABLE.d: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the Parachute simulation

SIM_PLD_ENABLE.d: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the Preland simulation

SIM_PLD_HEIGHT.n: Precland device center's height SITL origin
SIM_PLD_HEIGHT.d: Precland device center's height above SITL origin. Assumes a 2x2m square as station base

SIM_PLD_RATE.d: Precland device rate. e.g led patter refresh rate, RF message rate, etc.

SIM_PLD_SHIP.d: This makes the position of the landing beacon follow the simulated ship from SIM_SHIP. The ship movement is controlled with the SIM_SHIP parameters

SIM_PLD_TYPE.d: Precland device radiance type: it can be a cylinder, a cone, or a sphere.

SIM_PLD_YAW.n: Precland device systems rotation from north

SIM_RICH_CTRL.d: The pin number that the RichenPower spinner servo is connected to. (start at 1)

SIM_RICH_ENABLE.d: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the RichenPower simulator

SIM_SAIL_TYPE.d: 0: mainsail with sheet, 1: directly actuated wing

SIM_SB_ARM_LEN.d: distance from center of mass to one motor

SIM_SB_COL.d: center of lift position above CoG

SIM_SB_FLR.d: amount of additional lift generated by the helper balloon (for the purpose of ascent), as a proportion of the 'neutral buoyancy' lift

SIM_SB_MASS.d: mass of blimp not including lifting gas

SIM_SB_MOT_THST.d: thrust at max throttle for one motor

SIM_SB_YAW_RT.d: maximum yaw rate with full left throttle at target altitude

SIM_SHOVE_TIME.d: Force to the vehicle over a period of time

SIM_SHOVE_Y.d: Acceleration of shove to vehicle in y axis

SIM_SHOVE_Z.d: Acceleration of shove to vehicle in z axis

SIM_SLUP_DRAG.d: Slung Payload drag coefficient. Higher values increase drag and slow the payload more quickly

SIM_SLUP_LINELEN.d: Slung Payload line length in meters

SIM_SLUP_SYSID.d: Slung Payload MAVLink system id to distinguish it from others on the same network

SIM_SONAR_GLITCH.d: Probablility a sonar glitch would happen

SIM_SONAR_POS_Y.d: XYZ position of the sonar relative to the body frame origin (Y-axis)

SIM_SONAR_RND.d: Scaling factor for simulated sonar noise

SIM_SPR_ENABLE.d: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the Sprayer simulation

SIM_TA_ENABLE.d: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the simulated tonealarm

SIM_TEMP_BFACTOR.d: A pressure change with temperature that closely matches what has been observed with a ICM-20789

SIM_TEMP_BRD_OFF.d: Barometer board temperature offset from atmospheric temperature

SIM_TETH_DENSITY.d: Linear mass density of the tether wire

SIM_TETH_DMPCNST.d: Damping constant for the tether to simulate resistance based on change in stretch

SIM_TETH_ENABLE.d: Enable or disable the tether simulation

SIM_TETH_LINELEN.d: Maximum length of the tether line in meters

SIM_TETH_SPGCNST.d: Spring constant for the tether to simulate elastic forces when stretched beyond its maximum length

SIM_TETH_STUCK.d: Enable or disable a stuck tether simulation

SIM_TETH_SYSID.d: MAVLink system ID for the tether simulation, used to distinguish it from other systems on the network

SIM_THML_SCENARI.d: Scenario for thermalling simulation, for soaring

SIM_TIDE_DIR.d: Tide direction wave is coming from

SIM_TIME_JITTER.d: Upper limit of random jitter in loop time

SIM_TWIST_TIME.d: Time that twist is applied on the vehicle

SIM_TWIST_X.d: Rotational acceleration of twist x axis

SIM_UART_LOSS.d: Sets percentage of outgoing byte loss on UARTs

SIM_VIB_FREQ_X.d: Frequency of vibration applied to IMU readings in SITL (X-axis)

SIM_VIB_FREQ_Y.d: Frequency of vibration applied to IMU readings in SITL (Y-axis)

SIM_WIND_TURB.d: Allows you to emulate random wind variations in sim

SIM_WIND_T_ALT.d: Altitude at which wind reaches full strength, decaying from full strength as altitude lowers to ground level

SIM_WOW_PIN.d: SITL set this simulated pin to true if vehicle is on ground

SLUP_DEBUG.d: Slung payload debug output, set to 1 to enable debug

SLUP_DIST_MAX.d: Oscillation is suppressed when vehicle and payload are no more than this distance horizontally. Set to 0 to always suppress

SLUP_RESTOFS_TC.n: Slung Payload resting offset estimate filter time constant

SLUP_SYSID.d: Slung Payload mavlink system id. 0 to use any/all system ids

SLUP_VEL_P.d: Slung Payload Velocity P gain, higher values will result in faster movements in sync with payload

SLUP_WP_POS_P.n: Slung Payload return to WP position P gain
SLUP_WP_POS_P.d: WP position P gain. higher values will result in vehicle moving more quickly back to the original waypoint

STARTUP_DELAY.n: Delay before first servo movement from trim
STARTUP_DELAY.d: This parameter can be used to force the servos to their trim value for a time on startup. This can help with some servo types

START_LATITUDE.d: Combined with START_LONGITUDE this parameter allows for an initial position of the tracker to be set. This position will be used until the GPS gets lock. It can also be used to run a stationary tracker with no GPS attached.

START_LONGITUDE.d: Combined with START_LATITUDE this parameter allows for an initial position of the tracker to be set. This position will be used until the GPS gets lock. It can also be used to run a stationary tracker with no GPS attached.

STAT_BOOTCNT.d: Number of times board has been booted

STAT_DISTFLWN.d: Estimate of total distance flown since statistics reset

STAT_RESET.d: Seconds since January 1st 2016 (Unix epoch+1451606400) since statistics reset (set to 0 to reset statistics, other set values will be ignored)

SYSID_MYGCS.d: The identifier of the ground station in the MAVLink protocol. Don't change this unless you also modify the ground station to match.

SYSID_TARGET.d: The identifier of the vehicle being tracked. This should be zero (to auto detect) or be the same as the MAV_SYSID parameter of the vehicle being tracked.

SYSID_THISMAV.d: Allows setting an individual system id for this vehicle to distinguish it from others on the same network
SYSID_THISMAV.n: MAVLink system ID of this vehicle

TA_ACT_FN.d: Setting an RC channel's _OPTION to this value will use it for Terrain Avoidance enable/disable

TA_ALT_MAX.d: This is a limit on how high the terrain avoidane will take the vehicle. It acts a failsafe to prevent vertical flyaways.

TA_CMTC_ENABLE.d: Whether to enable Can't Make That Climb while running Terrain Avoidance

TA_CMTC_HGT.d: The minimum Height above terrain to maintain when following an AUTO mission or RTL. If zero(0) use TA_PTCH_DOW_MIN.

TA_CMTC_RAD.d: Use this radius for the loiter when trying to gain altitude. If not set or <=0 use WP_LOITER_RAD

TA_GSP_AIRBRAKE.d: This is the limit for triggering airbrake to slow groundspeed as a difference between the airspeed and groundspeed. -1 for disabled.

TA_GSP_MAX.d: This is a limit on how fast in groundspeeed terrain avoidance will take the vehicle. This is to allow for reliable sensor readings. -1 for disabled.

TA_HOME_DIST.d: Terrain avoidance will not be applied if the vehicle is less than this distance from home

TA_PTCH_DWN_MIN.d: If the downward distance is less than this value then start Pitching up to gain altitude.

TA_PTCH_FWD_MIN.d: If the farwardward distance is less than this value then start Pitching up to gain altitude.

TA_PTCH_GSP_MIN.d: Minimum Groundspeed (not airspeed) to be flying for Pitching to be used.

TA_PTCH_TIMEOUT.d: Minimum down or forward distance must be triggered for more than this many seconds to start Pitching

TA_QUAD_DWN_MIN.d: If the downward distance is less than this value then start Quading up to gain altitude.

TA_QUAD_FWD_MIN.d: If the farwardward distance is less than this value then start Quading up to gain altitude.

TEMP10_ADDR.d: Temperature sensor address, typically used for I2C address

TEMP10_BUS.d: Temperature sensor bus number, typically used to select from multiple I2C buses

TEMP10_MSG_ID.d: Sets the message device ID this backend listens for

TEMP10_PIN.n: Temperature sensor analog voltage sensing pin
TEMP10_PIN.d: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for temprature monitoring. Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins".

TEMP10_RTD_NOM.d: Nominal RTD resistance used to calculate temperature, typically 100 or 1000 ohms.

TEMP10_RTD_REF.d: Reference resistance used to calculate temperature, in ohms

TEMP10_SRC.d: Sensor Source is used to designate which device's temperature report will be replaced by this temperature sensor's data. If 0 (None) then the data is only available via log. In the future a new Motor temperature report will be created for returning data directly.

TEMP10_SRC_ID.d: Sensor Source Identification is used to replace a specific instance of a system component's temperature report with the temp sensor's. Examples: TEMP_SRC = 1 (ESC), TEMP_SRC_ID = 1 will set the temp of ESC1. TEMP_SRC = 3 (BatteryIndex),TEMP_SRC_ID = 2 will set the temp of BATT2. TEMP_SRC = 4 (BatteryId/SerialNum),TEMP_SRC_ID=42 will set the temp of all batteries that have param BATTn_SERIAL = 42.

TEMP8_PIN.d: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for temprature monitoring. Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins".

TEMP8_RTD_NOM.d: Nominal RTD resistance used to calculate temperature, typically 100 or 1000 ohms.

TEMP8_RTD_REF.d: Reference resistance used to calculate temperature, in ohms

TEMP8_SRC.d: Sensor Source is used to designate which device's temperature report will be replaced by this temperature sensor's data. If 0 (None) then the data is only available via log. In the future a new Motor temperature report will be created for returning data directly.

TEMP8_SRC_ID.d: Sensor Source Identification is used to replace a specific instance of a system component's temperature report with the temp sensor's. Examples: TEMP_SRC = 1 (ESC), TEMP_SRC_ID = 1 will set the temp of ESC1. TEMP_SRC = 3 (BatteryIndex),TEMP_SRC_ID = 2 will set the temp of BATT2. TEMP_SRC = 4 (BatteryId/SerialNum),TEMP_SRC_ID=42 will set the temp of all batteries that have param BATTn_SERIAL = 42.

TEMP9_A0.d: a0 in polynomial of form temperature in deg = a0 + a1*voltage + a2*voltage^2 + a3*voltage^3 + a4*voltage^4 + a5*voltage^5

TEMP9_A1.d: a1 in polynomial of form temperature in deg = a0 + a1*voltage + a2*voltage^2 + a3*voltage^3 + a4*voltage^4 + a5*voltage^5

TEMP9_A2.d: a2 in polynomial of form temperature in deg = a0 + a1*voltage + a2*voltage^2 + a3*voltage^3 + a4*voltage^4 + a5*voltage^5

TEMP9_A3.d: a3 in polynomial of form temperature in deg = a0 + a1*voltage + a2*voltage^2 + a3*voltage^3 + a4*voltage^4 + a5*voltage^5

TEMP9_A4.d: a4 in polynomial of form temperature in deg = a0 + a1*voltage + a2*voltage^2 + a3*voltage^3 + a4*voltage^4 + a5*voltage^5

TEMP9_A5.d: a5 in polynomial of form temperature in deg = a0 + a1*voltage + a2*voltage^2 + a3*voltage^3 + a4*voltage^4 + a5*voltage^5

TEMP9_ADDR.d: Temperature sensor address, typically used for I2C address

TEMP9_BUS.d: Temperature sensor bus number, typically used to select from multiple I2C buses

TEMP9_MSG_ID.d: Sets the message device ID this backend listens for

TEMP9_PIN.n: Temperature sensor analog voltage sensing pin
TEMP9_PIN.d: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for temprature monitoring. Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins".

TEMP9_RTD_NOM.d: Nominal RTD resistance used to calculate temperature, typically 100 or 1000 ohms.

TEMP9_RTD_REF.d: Reference resistance used to calculate temperature, in ohms

TEMP9_SRC.d: Sensor Source is used to designate which device's temperature report will be replaced by this temperature sensor's data. If 0 (None) then the data is only available via log. In the future a new Motor temperature report will be created for returning data directly.

v: Log only instances with sensor source set to None

TERR_BRK_ALT.d: terrain brake altitude. The altitude above the ground below which BRAKE mode will be engaged if in LOITER mode.

TERR_BRK_HDIST.d: terrain brake home distance. The distance from home where the auto BRAKE will be enabled. When within this distance of home the script will not activate

TERR_BRK_SPD.d: terrain brake speed threshold. Don't trigger BRAKE if both horizontal speed and descent rate are below this threshold. By setting this to a small value this can be used to allow the user to climb up to a safe altitude in LOITER mode. A value of 0.5 is recommended if you want to use LOITER to recover from an emergency terrain BRAKE mode change.

THR_KILL_CHAN.n: output channel to change on throttle kill
THR_KILL_CHAN.d: output channel to change on throttle kill, a value of zero disables the feature

THR_KILL_DEF.d: throttle kill default value. The default auxilliary function position on boot

THR_KILL_FUNC.d: AUX function to kill engine. This can be activated either with a RCn_OPTION and a R/C switch or with a ground station auxilliary function

THR_KILL_VAL.d: auxilliary value to kill throttle. Set to 2 to kill the throttle when the auxilliary is high. Set to 0 to kill when auxilliary is low

TOFSENSE_ID1.d: First TOFSENSE-M sensor ID. Leave this at 0 to accept all IDs and if only one sensor is present. You can change ID of sensor from NAssistant Software

TOFSENSE_ID2.d: Second TOFSENSE-M sensor ID. This cannot be 0. You can change ID of sensor from NAssistant Software

TOFSENSE_ID3.d: Third TOFSENSE-M sensor ID. This cannot be 0. You can change ID of sensor from NAssistant Software

TOFSENSE_INST1.d: First TOFSENSE-M sensors backend Instance. Setting this to 1 will pick the first backend from PRX_ or RNG_ Parameters (Depending on TOFSENSE_PRX)

TOFSENSE_INST2.d: Second TOFSENSE-M sensors backend Instance. Setting this to 2 will pick the second backend from PRX_ or RNG_ Parameters (Depending on TOFSENSE_PRX)

TOFSENSE_INST3.d: Third TOFSENSE-M sensors backend Instance. Setting this to 3 will pick the second backend from PRX_ or RNG_ Parameters (Depending on TOFSENSE_PRX)

TOFSENSE_MODE.d: TOFSENSE-M mode to be used. 0 for 8x8 mode. 1 for 4x4 mode

TOFSENSE_NO.d: Number of TOFSENSE-M CAN sensors connected

TOFSENSE_PRX.n: TOFSENSE-M to be used as Proximity sensor
TOFSENSE_PRX.d: Set 0 if sensor is to be used as a 1-D rangefinder (minimum of all distances will be sent, typically used for height detection). Set 1 if it should be used as a 3-D proximity device (Eg. Obstacle Avoidance)

TOFSENSE_S1_BR.d: Serial Port baud rate. Sensor baud rate can be changed from Nassistant software

TOFSENSE_S1_PRX.n: TOFSENSE-M to be used as Proximity sensor
TOFSENSE_S1_PRX.d: Set 0 if sensor is to be used as a 1-D rangefinder (minimum of all distances will be sent, typically used for height detection). Set 1 if it should be used as a 3-D proximity device (Eg. Obstacle Avoidance)

TOFSENSE_S1_SP.d: UART instance sensor is connected to. Set 1 if sensor is connected to the port with fist SERIALx_PROTOCOL = 28.

TRIK_ACT_FN.d: Setting an RC channel's _OPTION to this value will use it for trick action (abort,announce,execute)

TRIK_COUNT.d: Number of tricks which can be selected over the range of the trik selection RC channel

TRIK_ENABLE.d: Enables Tricks on Switch. TRIK params hidden until enabled

TRIK_SEL_FN.d: Setting an RC channel's _OPTION to this value will use it for trick selection

VID1_IPADDR0.d: Video stream IP Address first octet

VID1_IPADDR1.d: Video stream IP Address second octet

VID1_IPADDR2.d: Video stream IP Address third octet

VID1_IPADDR3.d: Video stream IP Address fourth octet

VID1_IPPORT.n: Camera1 Video Stream IP Address Port

VISO_DELAY_MS.d: Visual odometry sensor delay relative to inertial measurements

VISO_POS_M_NSE.d: Visual odometry position measurement noise minimum (meters). This value will be used if the sensor provides a lower noise value (or no noise value)

VISO_POS_X.n: Visual odometry camera X position offset
VISO_POS_X.d: X position of the camera in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin.

VISO_POS_Y.n: Visual odometry camera Y position offset
VISO_POS_Y.d: Y position of the camera in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin.

VISO_POS_Z.n: Visual odometry camera Z position offset
VISO_POS_Z.d: Z position of the camera in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin.

VISO_QUAL_MIN.d: Visual odometry will only be sent to EKF if over this value. -1 to always send (even bad values), 0 to send if good or unknown

VISO_SCALE.d: Visual odometry scaling factor applied to position estimates from sensor

VISO_VEL_M_NSE.d: Visual odometry velocity measurement noise in m/s

VISO_YAW_M_NSE.d: Visual odometry yaw measurement noise minimum (radians), This value will be used if the sensor provides a lower noise value (or no noise value)

VTX_ENABLE.n: Is the Video Transmitter enabled or not
VTX_ENABLE.d: Toggles the Video Transmitter on and off

VTX_FREQ.d: Video Transmitter Frequency. The frequency is derived from the setting of BAND and CHANNEL

VTX_MAX_POWER.d: Video Transmitter Maximum Power Level. Different VTXs support different power levels, this prevents the power aux switch from requesting too high a power level. The switch supports 6 power levels and the selected power will be a subdivision between 0 and this setting.

VTX_OPTIONS.d: Video Transmitter Options. Pitmode puts the VTX in a low power state. Unlocked enables certain restricted frequencies and power levels. Do not enable the Unlocked option unless you have appropriate permissions in your jurisdiction to transmit at high power levels. One stop-bit may be required for VTXs that erroneously mimic iNav behaviour.
b: Add leading zero byte to requests
Ignore status updates in CRSF and blindly set VTX options

VTX_POWER.d: Video Transmitter Power Level. Different VTXs support different power levels, the power level chosen will be rounded down to the nearest supported power level

WEB_BLOCK_SIZE.d: web server block size for download

WEB_SENDFILE_MIN.n: web server minimum file size for sendfile
WEB_SENDFILE_MIN.d: sendfile is an offloading mechanism for faster file download. If this is non-zero and the file is larger than this size then sendfile will be used for file download

WINCH_RC_FUNC.d: RCn_OPTION number to use to control winch rate

YAW2SRV_D.d: Yaw axis controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired yaw angle (heading) vs actual yaw angle

YAW2SRV_D_FF.d: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target

YAW2SRV_FLTD.n: Yaw axis controller derivative frequency in Hz
YAW2SRV_FLTD.d: Yaw axis controller derivative frequency in Hz

YAW2SRV_FLTE.n: Yaw axis controller error frequency in Hz
YAW2SRV_FLTE.d: Yaw axis controller error frequency in Hz

YAW2SRV_FLTT.n: Yaw axis controller target frequency in Hz
YAW2SRV_FLTT.d: Yaw axis controller target frequency in Hz

YAW2SRV_I.d: Yaw axis controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired yaw angle (heading) vs actual yaw angle

YAW2SRV_IMAX.n: Yaw axis controller I gain maximum
YAW2SRV_IMAX.d: Yaw axis controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum pwm change that the I gain will output

YAW2SRV_P.d: Yaw axis controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired yaw angle (heading) and actual yaw angle into a yaw servo pwm change

YAW2SRV_PDMX.n: Yaw axis controller PD sum maximum
YAW2SRV_PDMX.d: Yaw axis controller PD sum maximum. The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output

YAW2SRV_SMAX.d: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

YAW_RANGE.d: Yaw axis total range of motion in degrees

YAW_SLEW_TIME.n: Time for yaw to slew through its full range
YAW_SLEW_TIME.d: This controls how rapidly the tracker will change the servo output for yaw. It is set as the number of seconds to do a full rotation. You can use this parameter to slow the trackers movements, which may help with some types of trackers. A value of zero will allow for unlimited servo movement per update.

YAW_TRIM.d: Amount of extra yaw to add when tracking. This allows for small adjustments for an out of trim compass.
